chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever lends a man a loan until he becomes affluent (pays it back), his wealth is in zakat, and he is in prayer with the angels until he pays it back.

key_terms.يَقْضِيَهُ: he pays it back / fulfills it

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for lending money to someone in need according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the immense spiritual merit of qard al-hasan (benevolent loan), equating the lender's continuous reward to that of a worshipper in prayer alongside the angels. This tradition underscores the concept of 'sadaqah in situ,' where the capital remains active in generating spiritual merit until the debt is settled, reflecting the Shia emphasis on social welfare and the sanctity of fulfilling financial obligations.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who lends a loan to a man up to the time he becomes affluent, his (lender’s) wealth would be in Zakāt, he would be in the Salāt along with the Angels until he (the borrower) fulfils it (pays back the loan)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir who has said the following: “
If one lends a loan to a man until he becomes able to pay back, his (lender’s) money is in Zakat and he is in Salah (prayer) with the angels until the loan is paid back.’”
